column47: The Graduate School of Arts and Science (GSAS) offers more than 50 Master's programs, including the MA, MS, and MFA degrees. Most of these programs are designed for students who are preparing for doctoral study, but some are also designed to prepare students for specific careers or to enhance their professional credentials. GSAS also offers more than 10 dual-degree programs in collaboration with other NYU schools. The majority of these are master's programs.

The online application form, along with the application fee, is typically the first step. You will then be asked to upload or submit additional materials as outlined below. Always refer to your desired program's page for specific details, as requirements may vary.

Transcripts: Unofficial transcripts from each college or university where you have earned a degree, or from which you have received credit for courses that you wish to have count toward your graduate degree at NYU, are required for the application process. Official transcripts will be required upon admission.

Letters of Recommendation: Most departments require three letters of recommendation from faculty or others qualified to evaluate your academic and professional abilities. Please consult the specific program to which you are applying for further details on the number of letters and the type of information that is expected. Recommenders upload their letters directly to the online application system.

Statement of Academic Purpose: This required statement should be a concise essay of approximately 500 words (or two pages double-spaced) that describes your primary academic and research interests, your experiences, and your objectives.

Resume/Curriculum Vitae: Required for all applicants.

Test Scores:
GRE General Test: Many departments require the Graduate Record Examinations (GRE) General Test. Some departments require a GRE Subject Test. For master's programs in the sciences and social sciences, the GRE General Test may be optional or required. Please check your desired program's page for specifics.
English Language Proficiency Test: All applicants are required to demonstrate proficiency in English to be considered for admission. Proficiency can be demonstrated in one of the following ways: TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo, or PTE Academic, or by meeting exemption criteria.

Writing Sample: Required only by specific programs. Please consult the specific program to which you are applying for further details.

Online Application
You will submit the online application where you will upload the following:
*   Resume: Upload your most current professional resume, including your work history, education, volunteer work, and extracurricular activities.
*   Essays: Answer the essay questions provided in the online application. We learn more about your unique personality, professional goals, and decision-making skills through these essays.
*   Letters of Recommendation: You will be required to submit two letters of recommendation. One letter must be from a current or previous supervisor. The second letter may be from an additional supervisor, or someone who can speak to your professional strengths, such as a client or a professor.
*   Transcripts: Upload unofficial transcripts from all colleges and universities you have attended in the education section of the online application. If admitted, official transcripts from all degree-granting institutions will be required.
*   Standardized Tests (GMAT/GRE): The GMAT or GRE is required for all applicants. An official GMAT or GRE score report is required by the application deadline. Please have your official scores sent to NYU Stern using the following codes: GMAT (ZT2-R0-38) and GRE (2582). Stern does not have a minimum score requirement. Waiver for CPA-Eligible Applicants: Applicants who have passed all four sections of the CPA exam may be eligible for a GMAT/GRE waiver. More information regarding the waiver and eligibility criteria is available in the online application.
*   Application Fee: A $120 non-refundable application fee is required and must be paid online via credit card. Waivers are available in specific circumstances, including U.S. military personnel and members of certain organizations.

column47: The NYU Stern Master of Science in Accounting (MS in Accounting) program is designed for students who want to become licensed certified public accountants (CPAs). Students will develop a deep understanding of the global financial reporting environment, tax, audit, and financial advisory. The MS in Accounting curriculum prepares students for careers in public accounting, corporate finance, and consulting, among other fields. Students acquire the analytical, critical thinking, and communication skills necessary to succeed in a dynamic business environment. A 12-month full-time curriculum is offered to both recent college graduates and those with limited work experience.

column47: The Master of Fine Arts (MFA) in Studio Art program provides an intensive course of study in studio art through the development of professional artistic practice combined with critical research and engagement with contemporary art issues and theory. The program encourages diverse approaches to art-making that challenge disciplinary boundaries, providing opportunities to pursue a broad range of contemporary practices and research topics across art, design, and new media. The Department of Art provides an expansive, interdisciplinary environment that fosters experimentation and innovation within a challenging and supportive atmosphere. Students work closely with faculty mentors, developing strong independent studio practices, and engaging in critical dialogue with peers, faculty, and visiting artists. Students generally select one or two primary areas of focus during their studies. These areas are: Ceramics, Drawing, Painting, Photography, Print Media, Sculpture, and Transmedia (Art and Technology). The three-year program includes 60 credit hours of graduate course work, including graduate seminars, studio courses, and two required teaching assistantships. Students must also complete an MFA thesis project and exhibition.

column47: At NYU Rory Meyers College of Nursing, our Master of Science in Nursing (MSN) program is designed to provide registered nurses with the advanced knowledge and skills necessary to excel in a wide range of specialized practice areas. As a leading institution in nursing education, we are committed to preparing the next generation of nurse leaders, clinicians, and educators to address complex healthcare challenges and improve patient outcomes. Choosing NYU Meyers for your MSN means joining a community dedicated to innovation, research, and compassionate care. Our program offers: Specialized Advanced Practice Areas (diverse concentrations such as Adult-Gerontology, Psychiatric-Mental Health, Pediatric Primary Care, Nurse-Midwifery, Women’s Health, Nursing Administration, and Nursing Education); Expert Faculty (nationally recognized leaders in nursing who bring extensive clinical experience and research expertise to the classroom); Cutting-Edge Curriculum (engage with evidence-based practices, advanced clinical skills, and theoretical frameworks that prepare you for leadership roles); Flexible Learning Options (explore full-time and part-time study options designed to accommodate your professional and personal commitments); Clinical Excellence (gain hands-on experience in top healthcare settings across New York City, working with diverse patient populations and interprofessional teams); Career Advancement (position yourself for advanced roles in healthcare, including nurse practitioner, nurse-midwife, administrator, or educator).

The Doctor of Philosophy in Psychology program is a research-oriented program designed to train future psychologists for careers in research and academe. Graduates of the program are expected to make significant contributions to the field of psychology in terms of research, theory building, and application.
The PhD in Clinical Psychology prepares students for the practice of clinical psychology and for leadership roles in mental health service delivery, research, and policy formulation. Students are trained in assessment, diagnosis, and psychotherapy within the scientist-practitioner model.
The PhD in Developmental Psychology focuses on advanced scholarship and research in the scientific study of human development across the lifespan. It emphasizes developmental processes within their socio-cultural context, particularly in the Philippine setting.
The PhD in Social-Cultural Psychology focuses on advanced scholarship and research in social and cultural aspects of human behavior. It emphasizes the dynamic interplay of individual, social, and cultural factors in shaping psychological processes and outcomes, particularly in the Philippine setting.

column47: Our PhD in Counseling Psychology prepares students to become leading researchers, university faculty, and practitioners dedicated to promoting social justice and human rights, especially for marginalized populations. We emphasize an understanding of the individual within family, community, and cultural contexts, and the importance of ecological and systemic approaches to intervention, prevention, and training. The PhD in Counseling Psychology is an APA-accredited program designed to prepare students for careers as counseling psychologists in academic, research, and applied settings. Our program is committed to a scientist-practitioner model of training, emphasizing the integration of scientific inquiry and clinical practice. We prepare students to conduct research that contributes to the scientific understanding of human behavior and to apply evidence-based interventions in diverse contexts. The program provides comprehensive training in psychological assessment, diagnosis, intervention, consultation, and supervision, with a strong emphasis on cultural competence and social justice. Students develop expertise in various theoretical orientations, research methodologies, and professional ethics. Through coursework, practicum experiences, and dissertation research, students cultivate the skills necessary for ethical and effective practice and for advancing the field of counseling psychology.

Graduates are prepared to translate research into practice, lead quality improvement initiatives, and develop innovative healthcare delivery models. The DNP program prepares students for the highest level of nursing practice and provides the knowledge and skills necessary to improve patient outcomes and transform healthcare. Through a rigorous curriculum and extensive clinical experiences, students develop expertise in areas such as advanced health assessment, pathophysiology, pharmacology, data analysis, and program evaluation. The program emphasizes interprofessional collaboration and ethical leadership to address complex healthcare challenges.

column47: The Master of Science (MS) in Biology offers students the opportunity to advance their knowledge and skills in various fields of modern biology. The program provides a broad foundation in fundamental biological principles and offers opportunities for specialization through coursework and research. It is designed for students interested in pursuing further graduate studies (including Ph.D. programs), careers in research, biotechnology, health-related fields, environmental science, or education. The program offers both a thesis and non-thesis option. Students in the thesis option complete original research under the guidance of a faculty mentor, culminating in a written thesis and oral defense. The non-thesis option requires a broader range of coursework and can culminate in a capstone project or comprehensive examination. Both options emphasize critical thinking, scientific communication, and advanced laboratory skills, preparing students for diverse professional paths in biology.

This program provides students with a strong foundation in core biomedical engineering principles, along with opportunities to specialize in various sub-disciplines such as biomechanics, biomaterials, medical imaging, neural engineering, and computational biomedical engineering. Graduates are prepared for careers in research and development, academia, and industry within the healthcare and biotechnology sectors. The curriculum emphasizes both theoretical knowledge and practical skills through coursework, laboratory experiences, and thesis or project options. Students will learn to apply engineering principles to solve complex problems in biology and medicine, contributing to advancements in diagnostics, therapeutics, and healthcare technologies.

column47: The Master of Science in Biomedical Engineering (MSBE) with a specialization in Medical Physics is a 30-credit, CAMPEP-accredited program offered in collaboration with the NYU Grossman School of Medicine. Our curriculum educates students in the fundamental physics of medical imaging and radiation therapy while training them to use the latest technologies and research to develop innovative solutions for global health and medical challenges. Rooted in applied physics, mathematics, chemistry, and biology, medical physics uses an engineering approach to address challenges in medicine and human health. Our graduates are prepared for careers in industry, research, and academia. The program can be completed in two years of full-time study, or students can elect to pursue the degree part-time. Our graduates are well-prepared for entry into residency programs in therapeutic medical physics, diagnostic medical physics, nuclear medical physics, or careers in industry. The program is specifically designed to meet the academic requirements for certification in Medical Physics by the American Board of Radiology (ABR).

The GRE General Test is optional for all PhD and MS applicants for Spring 2024 and Fall 2024 admissions. Applicants for doctoral programs usually possess a master’s degree in engineering or a related discipline prior to admission. However, highly qualified applicants with a bachelor’s degree in engineering or a related field may be considered for direct admission to a PhD program. column47: The Medical Physics PhD Track is a specialization within the Biomedical Engineering PhD Program offered at NYU Tandon School of Engineering. This interdisciplinary PhD track is designed for students interested in pursuing research and a career in medical physics. Our program emphasizes rigorous training in the fundamental principles and clinical applications of medical physics, preparing students to excel in academic, clinical, and industrial settings. Our curriculum offers a unique blend of engineering, physics, and medical coursework, providing students with a comprehensive understanding of imaging, radiation therapy, and related technologies. Students conduct research under the mentorship of faculty from the Department of Radiation Oncology and other departments within NYU Langone Health, as well as faculty from the NYU Tandon School of Engineering. Upon graduation, students are well-prepared for careers as medical physicists in hospitals, research institutions, and industry, or for postdoctoral fellowships leading to academic positions. Graduates are also qualified to pursue residency training in medical physics, which is a requirement for certification by the American Board of Radiology (ABR).

column47: Our MS in Biomedical Informatics program, offered through NYU Langone Health, is designed for those seeking to gain expertise in the field of biomedical informatics, whether for a career as a practicing informaticist or to apply informatics principles to their primary field. Our program is highly selective and provides comprehensive training in biomedical informatics, including clinical informatics, translational bioinformatics, and public health informatics. column47:
Materials science and engineering is an interdisciplinary field built on the basic sciences of physics, chemistry and mathematics, as well as the engineering sciences. It focuses on the fundamental relationships between the processing, structure, properties and performance of materials, and encompasses all classes of materials, including metals, ceramics, polymers, semiconductors, composites and biomaterials. The Materials Engineering MS program at NYU Tandon School of Engineering offers a comprehensive curriculum that integrates the various facets of materials science and engineering and provides students with a strong foundation in both the fundamentals and practical applications of the field.

The program is designed to prepare students for careers in research and development, manufacturing, and technical management in a wide range of industries, including aerospace, automotive, electronics, energy, biomedical, and advanced manufacturing. Graduates will be equipped to tackle complex challenges related to material selection, design, processing, characterization, and failure analysis.

Students will gain expertise in:
*   Material Characterization: Understanding and applying various experimental techniques to analyze the structure, composition, and properties of materials.
*   Mechanical Behavior of Materials: Investigating the response of materials to external forces, including elasticity, plasticity, fracture, and fatigue.
*   Thermodynamics and Kinetics of Materials: Applying principles of thermodynamics and kinetics to understand phase transformations, diffusion, and reaction processes in materials.
*   Materials Processing: Learning about different manufacturing processes used to produce materials with desired properties, such as solidification, powder metallurgy, thin-film deposition, and additive manufacturing.
*   Computational Materials Science: Utilizing computational tools and simulations to predict material behavior and design new materials.
*   Advanced Materials: Exploring emerging materials such as nanomaterials, smart materials, and biomaterials, and their applications.

The curriculum is flexible, allowing students to tailor their studies to their specific interests through a selection of elective courses. Research opportunities with faculty are also available, providing students with hands-on experience in cutting-edge materials research.

The Sackler Institute at NYU Langone Health trains future leaders in biomedical research through graduate study in our seven PhD programs, an MD/PhD Program, and a variety of postdoctoral programs. Students benefit from the mentorship of more than 450 faculty members in 30 departments at NYU Grossman School of Medicine and other NYU schools and colleges who are pursuing biomedical research, with areas of expertise that include biochemistry, cell biology, genetics, molecular pharmacology, neuroscience, microbiology, immunology, and structural biology. column47:
The M.S. in Physics program provides a solid foundation in the core areas of physics while also allowing for some specialization. Students pursuing the M.S. degree at NYU typically do so for one of two reasons: either to strengthen their background in physics before applying to a Ph.D. program, or to acquire the knowledge base for a career in industry. The program can be completed with or without a thesis option.

M.S. students pursuing the non-thesis option complete a total of 32 points, or eight graduate courses. These courses include two required courses (General Physics I and II) and six elective courses. Electives can be taken from the range of graduate courses offered by the Department of Physics, in topics such as classical mechanics, quantum mechanics, electrodynamics, statistical mechanics, and more specialized areas like astrophysics, condensed matter physics, and particle physics.

M.S. students pursuing the thesis option also complete 32 points, which includes six graduate courses (24 points) and an M.S. thesis (8 points). The thesis involves original research conducted under the supervision of a faculty member and culminates in a written thesis and oral defense. The thesis option provides valuable research experience, often leading to publications, and is particularly beneficial for students considering doctoral studies.

Both options offer flexibility in course selection, allowing students to tailor their academic path to their interests and career goals. Students have access to state-of-the-art research facilities and opportunities to collaborate with leading faculty members on cutting-edge research projects.

column47: The Master of Public Administration (MPA) at NYU Wagner is one of the nation’s top graduate professional degrees. It prepares students from a wide range of backgrounds to be leaders who can translate ideas into action and move society forward. Our flexible curriculum allows students to gain the analytical and management skills necessary to be effective public service leaders, while also specializing in a policy area or management function of their choosing. You’ll learn how to analyze and shape policy; manage people, projects, and organizations; and communicate effectively with stakeholders. Our graduates are equipped to lead mission-driven organizations in government, nonprofits, and the private sector, in New York City and around the world.

column47: The Public Health Certificate provides an introduction to the core functions of public health and population health. This 12-credit certificate provides students with foundational knowledge in the disciplines of epidemiology, biostatistics, environmental health, social and behavioral sciences, and health policy and management. The certificate is designed for students seeking to gain a basic understanding of public health principles or those who wish to enhance their professional skills in areas related to population health. The certificate is especially useful for clinicians, social workers, educators, and other professionals who work with diverse populations.

NYU GPH’s online Master of Public Health program brings the entire public health field to you. Designed to accommodate the needs of working professionals, the rigorous program is rooted in the school’s core values of research, education, and service, ensuring you will graduate with the skills to address pressing public health issues.

As an online MPH student, you will learn the core disciplines of public health, along with topics in epidemiology, biostatistics, environmental health, health policy, and social and behavioral sciences. Students also choose one of three concentrations – custom-designed for the online format: Applied Biostatistics, Community Health, or Global Health. Our online MPH delivers a diverse and engaging curriculum that builds on your career experiences and prepares you for leadership roles in various public health fields.

column47: Designed for students with a professional degree, strong research interests, or prior experience in the field of public health, the Master of Science in Public Health (MSPH) program at NYU’s School of Global Public Health provides advanced methodological, analytical, and data-driven skills needed for public health practice and research. The MSPH enables students to deepen their understanding of critical public health issues while developing the leadership and communication skills necessary to create positive change within complex health systems. With hands-on opportunities to apply theory to real-world challenges, students gain the tools to design, implement, and evaluate public health interventions. The 45-credit MSPH program has a strong research and practice focus, enabling students to gain advanced methodological and analytic skills with a strong foundation in public health science. Students complete a 6-credit Applied Practice Experience (APEX) and an 8-credit Master’s Thesis (Capstone) as part of the curriculum. The program culminates in a comprehensive exam. Graduates are prepared for doctoral study or for leadership roles in diverse public health organizations.

column47: The Public Health Accelerated Master of Science in Public Health (MSPH) offers a rigorous academic experience to those interested in careers that require both depth and breadth of public health knowledge and competencies. The accelerated MSPH is designed to provide students with the foundational skills of public health and advanced knowledge in an area of concentration. Students pursuing the Public Health Accelerated MSPH program are eligible to pursue one of the following concentrations: Community Health Science and Practice, Epidemiology, Biostatistics, Environmental Public Health Sciences, Global Health, or Social and Behavioral Sciences. The program prepares students for various public health positions in governmental, non-governmental, and private sector organizations. The curriculum builds on a foundation in core public health disciplines and culminates in a 180-hour applied practice experience and a culminating experience that integrates knowledge across public health domains. The MSPH is an accelerated program designed for students with at least two years of full-time work experience or a master’s degree in a relevant field. This program is completed in 10 months and applicants must have a bachelor's degree to apply.

column47: The Master of Science (MS) in Public Policy is a two-year, 45-credit degree program for students seeking an intensive, analytical education focused on domestic public policy. The program provides a multidisciplinary social science education, developing students’ analytical and methodological skills to understand, analyze, and address domestic policy issues. Students learn to apply quantitative and qualitative methods to evaluate the causes, consequences, and effectiveness of public policies. The curriculum combines a common core with opportunities for specialization, offering students an in-depth understanding of the forces that shape public policy in specific policy domains.
